shape.description: Short open scoop. Low end is a tongue with slot; the other end curves UP to a rounded free lip, with no foot. Clips to one port and hangs free, tip above the port.
shape.sizeBasis: Rise about 1.5 block heights above the tongue and reach about 1.3 block widths, from uploads/T-14_1793563852236.jpg (clipped to a two-block stack). Perspective makes the reach the less certain number.

accepts: block cup end (top notch or joint hole) with its side tab

physics.behaviour: Not a downhill exit. Marble runs out of the port up the scoop, slows, and rolls back in. It re-enters that block and goes on: into the hole, or across. Tip rises above the port on all pages.

evidence.shows: tip well above grey top, low end at cup end
low end at joint, tip up
on M-04, tip up, T-08 on the adjacent face
Real piece clipped to a two-block stack: the lip rises about 1.5 block heights above the tongue

assumptions: Connection: the track end is a thin tongue that overlaps the next piece. A small slot in the tongue takes a small peg on that piece, and a hooked foot under the end drops into the block's side tab (photos IMG_0959, 0963; foot on trex_plans_02).
Up-and-back is inferred from shape and placement. extracted_trex.json calls it a slide dropping about 1 slot; every drawing shows the tip going up.

Scale is estimated, not measured: one cell = one block width (top-down maps, trex_plans_27). A cell of about 45 mm is judged from hand and laptop-key size in IMG_0960/0963, +-5 mm. No ruler was in any photo.
openQuestions: Roll a marble in: does it return, or does it hop out?
